The graph of the function $y=g(x)$ is shown above. 
Approximate ${g}^{′}(x)$ at the point $x=1$ using a forward difference approximation with step size $h=1.$ Do not round the answer.

${g}^{′}(1)≈$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
We use the forward difference approximation

$$
{g}^{′}(x)≈\frac{g(x+h)-g(x)}{h}
$$

 
at the point $x=1.$ Applying the above formula with $x=1$ and $h=1$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(1) & ≈\frac{g(1+1)-g(1)}{1} \\  & =\frac{g(2)-g(1)}{1} \\  & =\frac{2-4}{1} \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$
